## Classes

### <a name="vuls"></a>`vuls`

from PuppetDB.

A bare include installs a pinned Vuls release, builds its configuration from
every active Linux node in PuppetDB, and installs the scan as a systemd
service. Nothing scans on a schedule until `scan_schedule_enabled` is true;
until then `systemctl start vuls-scan.service` runs it by hand.

Linux nodes are scanned over SSH as `scan_login`, with host keys from
PuppetDB's ssh facts. Windows nodes are assessed through `vuls server` from
what PuppetDB and the `vuls_windows` fact already know, so nothing logs in to
them. `vuls::target` prepares a Linux node to be scanned.

When a scan has finished every step, the run it produced is recorded in
`/var/lib/vuls/last-complete-run`. Anything reading results on its own
schedule should read that run, not the newest directory.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
include vuls
```

##### Scheduled, with credentials

```puppet
class { 'vuls':
  scan_schedule_enabled => true,
  scan_ssh_private_key  => Sensitive('-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----...'),
}
```

##### <a name="-vuls--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `String[1]`

Vuls release to install.

Default value: `'0.40.1'`

##### <a name="-vuls--sha256"></a>`sha256`

Data type: `String[64, 64]`

SHA-256 of that release's linux_amd64 tarball, from its checksums.txt.

Default value: `'31fc4660f3266916f8d4fb30c2c4a5477a912f0178573853f4ce19dd2a1f91f4'`

##### <a name="-vuls--scan_login"></a>`scan_login`

Data type: `String[1]`

The account Vuls logs in to Linux nodes as.

Default value: `'vuls'`

##### <a name="-vuls--scan_ssh_private_key"></a>`scan_ssh_private_key`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

The private key it logs in with. Without one, Linux nodes can't be scanned.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-vuls--exclude"></a>`exclude`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Certnames to leave out.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-vuls--exclude_patterns"></a>`exclude_patterns`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Regular expressions; a Linux node whose certname matches any is left out,
for whole networks the scanner can't reach.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-vuls--scan_schedule_enabled"></a>`scan_schedule_enabled`

Data type: `Boolean`

Run the scan on `scan_time`. Off by default.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-vuls--scan_time"></a>`scan_time`

Data type: `String[1]`

systemd OnCalendar for the scheduled scan.

Default value: `'*-*-* 02:15:00'`

##### <a name="-vuls--scan_condition"></a>`scan_condition`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

A command run as root before each scan; the scan is skipped when it exits
non-zero. For keeping out of another scanner's way.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-vuls--memory_max"></a>`memory_max`

Data type: `String[1]`

Hard memory ceiling for a run. Vuls's database is about 13 GB, and a run
over a few dozen nodes peaks around 6 GB.

Default value: `'8G'`

##### <a name="-vuls--keep_days"></a>`keep_days`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Days of results to keep.

Default value: `3`

### <a name="vuls--target"></a>`vuls::target`

Include this on the nodes you scan; the scanner itself takes `vuls`. It
creates the account Vuls logs in as, with the scan key's public half. It
reads the scanner's `vuls::scan_login`, so the login is set once for both.

Safe to include everywhere before the key exists: without it it warns and
changes nothing. On Windows it does nothing, because Vuls reads Windows nodes
from facts and never logs in to them.

To use an account that already exists, set `manage_user` to false, and the
class only adds the key.

#### Examples

##### In a profile every scanned node gets

```puppet
include vuls::target
```

##### Hiera, common to the scanner and the nodes

```puppet
vuls::target::ssh_public_key: "ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nza... vuls-scan"
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `vuls::target` class:

* [`ssh_public_key`](#-vuls--target--ssh_public_key)
* [`login`](#-vuls--target--login)
* [`manage_user`](#-vuls--target--manage_user)
* [`ssh_key_name`](#-vuls--target--ssh_key_name)

##### <a name="-vuls--target--ssh_public_key"></a>`ssh_public_key`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A(ssh|ecdsa|sk)-\S+ \S+/]]`

The whole line from the `.pub` file, such as `ssh-rsa AAAA... vuls-scan`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-vuls--target--login"></a>`login`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The account name. Defaults to `vuls::scan_login`, then `vuls`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-vuls--target--manage_user"></a>`manage_user`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to create the account. Set false for an account that already
exists or is managed elsewhere.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-vuls--target--ssh_key_name"></a>`ssh_key_name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The name of the authorised key, `<login>-vuls` by default. Declared with
stdlib's `ensure_resource`, so another module describing the same key under
the same name, such as a second scanner sharing this account, declares it
once. The same name for a different key fails the catalogue.

Default value: `undef`

## Functions

### <a name="vuls--puppetdb_rows"></a>`vuls::puppetdb_rows`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Runs a PuppetDB query, and answers with an empty list when PuppetDB is down or
the function isn't there at all. A scanner host should still converge the rest
of its catalogue when PuppetDB can't answer.

#### `vuls::puppetdb_rows(String[1] $query)`

Runs a PuppetDB query, and answers with an empty list when PuppetDB is down or
the function isn't there at all. A scanner host should still converge the rest
of its catalogue when PuppetDB can't answer.

Returns: `Any` The rows, or an empty list.

##### `query`

Data type: `String[1]`

The PQL query.
